messages:
sanjay: Quick heads-up — saw ~12% p99 latency regression on the non-chat reranker/emb endpoint after yesterday's kernel selector change. Profiling attached via perf-bot.

olivia: ugh, thanks. is this at peak qps or across the board?

sanjay: mostly at mid-high QPS (30–60k eps for that route). median fine, but p75->p99 gap widened. baseline run from two days ago looks clean.

perf-bot: profiling-summary: CPU hot funcs: kernel_dispatcher::select(28%), kv_cache::evict_scan(18%), slab_batcher::form_batches(14%). Flamegraph link: https://perf.example/runs/1845234700

mike: slab_batcher::form_batches at 14% is interesting — we've seen similar when token budgets are too tight and we end up with lots of tiny batches + more kernel switches. What are current token budget targets for the reranker route?

sanjay: token_budget_target=1024 (global non-chat default). We recently turned on kernel selection fallback which may prefer a slightly different execution path for short sequences.

jen: kv_cache::evict_scan at 18% smells like thrashing. Are we seeing lots of KV misses causing full reloads of the cache and therefore more kernel warmups? Any change in sequence distribution?

sanjay: good call. The recent traffic has more long-query tails — mean tokens per request rose from ~48 -> ~132 for that route. That pushes more KV entries and causes eviction churn.

katie: proposed quick experiment: 1) bump token_budget_target -> 2048 for reranker route only 2) increase kv cache size by 20% for the canary pool 3) change batch formation to bucket by token-span (slab window) instead of strict arrival time for 100ms window.

olivia: +1 to experiment. We should also capture kernel selection counts (fast path vs fallback) and batch size histograms. If small batches are the issue, moving to token-span bucketing should reduce kernel switches.

mike: config snippet to push to staging canary: ```
route: reranker-nonchat
continuous_batching:
  token_budget_target: 2048
  slab_allocator:
    mode: token-span
    max_window_ms: 100
kv_cache:
  size_percent_override: 120
kernel_selection:
  prefer_fastpath_threshold_tokens: 256
```

jen: also add a perf counter for 'kernel_switches_per_min' and 'evict_scan_count' so we can correlate.

sanjay: I'll deploy the canary to 2 hosts in staging at 11:30 PT with telemetry flags and enable perf counters. Will post updates.

perf-bot: canary-deploy: reranker-nonchat -> staging-canary (2 hosts) at 2026-03-17T11:30:00Z. Telemetry: perf_counters=true.

olivia: TL;DR for postmortem triage: likely combo of token distribution shift + kernelFallback path + kv thrash. Experiment looks good. If we see batch sizes shrink < 4 avg, revert.

sanjay: staging results: after 30m under a 40k eps replay — p99 improved by 9% vs yesterday's broken run, kernel_switches_per_min down 38%, evict_scan_count down 25%.

mike: nice! any regression on median latency or throughput?

sanjay: median unchanged, throughput stable. Memory bump on canary hosts ~+8% (expected).

katie: next step: roll to 10% production canary and add a kernel selector tweak: increase prefer_fastpath_threshold_tokens -> 512 to bias toward fast kernels for mid-length sequences.

jen: add a guard: automated rollback if p99 increases >5% or evict_scan_count rises.

sanjay: rolling 10% now. will report back in 1hr.

perf-bot: canary-rollout: 10% -> prod at 2026-03-17T12:45:00Z.

olivia: thanks team. once stable we should bake a reranker-specific default (not the global 1024). Also file a follow-up to revisit slab allocator heuristics so token-span isn't a special-case hack forever.

sanjay: agreed. creating follow-up ticket and will include microbenchmarks for different sequence distributions.
